A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with matching authors, dataset, model, and principal experiments. Text, equations, tables, and figures support reliable comparison. v1 ends after its references; v3 additionally contains readable supplementary Sections A-1–A-8.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark results, model ablations, synthetic-to-real adaptation experiments, and partial-sketch evaluations in Tables 2–3 and Figures 5–7.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds a user study, further ablations, robustness evaluations, an expertise comparison, and sampling-speed experiments.

M1.justification: Sections 3–4 retain the same synthetic-sketch pipeline, Fourier/BERT encoder, augmentations, frozen VQ-VAE, and SDFusion training objective. The additional ordering variants and reduced DDIM budgets are experimental comparisons, not replacements of the proposed method.

E1.justification: The original training coverage remains unchanged, but v3 adds reference-free sketches, explicit unsnapped-input evaluations, unseen ShapeNet categories, ModelNet objects, and expert-versus-beginner sketches. These substantially extend the evaluated input conditions, object categories, data sources, and sketcher populations.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains Luo et al. and LAS-Diffusion as its external baselines. However, Figure A-6 extends the real-test-set qualitative comparison to include LAS-Diffusion, whereas v1's Figure 4 compares only against Luo et al. This changes comparator participation within that qualitative evaluation.

E3.justification: Existing benchmark splits, geometric metrics, and training budgets remain unchanged. New protocols include a 40-sketch study with 38 participants providing 1,900 Likert ratings, comparison of expert and beginner drawings of 100 shapes, and evaluation at 10, 25, 50, and 100 DDIM steps.

E4.justification: v3 adds Fourier-feature ablations, DFS/BFS and ordering-perturbation tests, an order-aware versus order-agnostic partial-input comparison, snapping and unseen-class robustness analyses, expertise effects, and sampling tradeoffs. The original ablation table is retained, and the earlier completion-performance curve moves from Figure 7 to Figure A-1.

E5.justification: v1 reports a plus/minus quantity for generation time; v3 extends such reporting to human correspondence ratings in Table 3 and expertise-specific F-scores in Section A-6. The new quantities are not clearly identified as standard deviations, standard errors, or confidence intervals. No seed counts or formal significance tests are added.

E6.justification: The main benchmark scores and original ablation results are unchanged, but substantial new results appear. Free-hand ratings are 3.60±1.01 for the proposed method versus 2.02±0.89 for Luo et al.; BFS obtains 47.8 F-score versus 56.8 for the full model. New DDIM settings, expertise comparisons, and qualitative generalization successes and failures further expand the findings.

T1.justification: Equations 1–7 retain the same sketch tokenization, Fourier encodings, projections, and embedding combination. Neither version develops additional theorems or proofs; the supplement's ordering discussion provides empirical interpretation rather than new formal reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same three scientific contributions and claims about geometric fidelity, synthetic-to-real generalization, and partial-sketch performance. The new experiments support these claims without redefining their headline scope.

C2.justification: Section A-1 qualifies the ordering explanation: consistent sequential structure helps, without establishing that synthetic ordering models human drawing behavior. Section A-5 discusses furniture-prior failures on unseen objects, while A-6 proposes abstraction as an explanation for experts' lower reconstruction scores. These substantially expand mechanism interpretations and applicability boundaries.

D1.justification: The abstract changes data/model availability from a promised release to a stated completed release at the same project site. Table A-2 additionally specifies batch size 1 for timing. The core architecture, optimizer, training schedule, hardware, and training-time disclosures remain unchanged; external availability was not independently checked.

R1.justification: Section 2.3 adds focused discussion of classical sketch rendering and structured CAD/B-rep work, including CAD2Sketch, Text2CAD, and BrepGen. v3 also credits StrokeAggregator as inspiration for culling and adds dataset references. The central positioning against unordered point-cloud sketch encoders remains intact.

P1.justification: Most introductory, methodological, and concluding prose is retained. Changes include locally expanded related work, moving partial-sketch discussion into the supplement, introducing the free-hand study in the main text, and expanding acknowledgments. This is a localized reorganization rather than extensive rewriting of the existing narrative.

P2.justification: v3 adds user-study, additional-ablation, and sampling-tradeoff tables, together with substantial free-hand, unsnapped, unseen-class, and baseline-comparison image grids. Completion illustrations are reorganized and expanded, while the original completion curve is relocated. Table 1 moves and Table 2 receives a side-caption layout.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially addresses v1's limited validation of reference-free use and its incomplete explanation of why ordering helps. The user study, ordering perturbations, and explicit unseen-class failures strengthen both practical evidence and the boundaries of the central interpretation. Undefined plus/minus quantities and inconsistencies between Table A-2's timing units and claimed speedup weaken parts of the new reporting, but do not outweigh these substantive gains.
